skill.description: Build agent-facing web applications with ATXP authentication, MCP tools, Express APIs, SQLite cookie storage, and ClawDirect directory publishing patterns.
skill.summary: Create ATXP-enabled web apps that AI agents can use through browsers and MCP tools.
skill.author: napoleond

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown fences, TypeScript template literals, configuration examples, or reference links rather than hidden execution. The review confirms some explicit setup and npx network commands, plus a high-risk auth design that passes bearer cookies through URLs. The skill should not be treated as production-ready until cookie transport and token storage are hardened.

remediation.issue: Bearer authentication cookies are passed in URL query parameters.
remediation.suggestion: Use a short-lived one-time bootstrap code or POST-based exchange, then immediately invalidate it and scrub request logs.

remediation.issue: Raw cookie values are stored without expiry or revocation enforcement.
remediation.suggestion: Store hashed token digests, add expires_at and revoked_at fields, and enforce rotation during cookie validation.

remediation.issue: Example commands install packages and call external paid services.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, pin package versions where possible, and label costs before any command execution.

semantic_findings.title: Authentication Cookie Passed Through Query String
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends passing a browser authentication cookie as a URL query parameter and then redirecting. Bearer tokens in URLs can leak through server logs, browser history, analytics tools, screenshots, and referrer headers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple sections explicitly recommend the query-string cookie bootstrap. This is a known bearer-token exposure pattern even though it is framed as an agent browser workaround.

semantic_findings.title: Long-Lived Bearer Cookies Stored Without Expiry Enforcement
semantic_findings.description: The template stores raw cookie values in SQLite and sets a 30-day browser cookie, but the table schema and lookup flow do not enforce expiration, hashing, rotation, or revocation. A database disclosure could expose reusable authentication tokens.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The schema stores cookie_value directly and records only created_at. The validation function checks token equality without expiration or revocation logic.

content.value_statement: Agent-facing web apps need reliable authentication between MCP tools and browsers. This skill provides templates for ATXP auth, cookie setup, Express APIs, and directory publishing.
actual_capabilities: Scaffold Node.js and TypeScript projects for ATXP web apps.
Show Express cookie authentication linked to MCP tools.
Define @longrun/turtle MCP tools with optional ATXP payments.
Provide SQLite patterns for storing agent account cookies.
Create an agent skill template for browser and MCP workflows.
Document ClawDirect directory add, edit, and delete commands.
limitations: The examples need security hardening before production use.
The guidance assumes Node.js, Express, SQLite, and ATXP.
The skill does not generate a complete hosted application by itself.
Some example commands contact external services and may require payment.

use_cases.description: Create a browser authentication bridge for agents that already use MCP tools.

use_cases.description: Design MCP tools that require ATXP authentication and optional payment before execution.

use_cases.title: Publish an Agent Directory Entry
use_cases.description: Prepare a ClawDirect listing so agents can discover and call a web service.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use clawdirect-dev to outline an ATXP-enabled web app for my service. Include the MCP tools, browser flow, and storage choices.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use clawdirect-dev to design cookie authentication for my Express API. Explain the files, routes, and validation steps I need.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Paid Agent Action
prompt_templates.prompt: Use clawdirect-dev to add a paid MCP action to my app. Include authentication, payment handling, and clear user-facing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use clawdirect-dev to review my planned ATXP browser authentication flow. Identify deployment, logging, cookie, and payment risks.

output_examples.input: Plan an ATXP web app for a document review service.
output_examples.output: A project plan with MCP tools, browser login flow, protected API routes, storage choices, and deployment notes.

output_examples.input: Add browser authentication for agents that already call my MCP server.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step implementation outline for issuing cookies, validating requests, and redirecting agents after authentication.

output_examples.input: Prepare my app for ClawDirect publication.
output_examples.output: A publishing checklist covering the listing fields, thumbnail requirements, ownership rules, costs, and deletion behavior.

best_practices: Treat generated cookies as bearer credentials and protect them like secrets.
Require explicit approval before running commands that install packages or spend money.
Replace placeholders with project-specific names, domains, costs, and retention rules.
anti_patterns: Do not use query strings for long-lived authentication tokens in production.
Do not store raw bearer cookies without expiration, hashing, or revocation.
Do not publish paid MCP tools without clear cost and confirmation behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build ATXP-enabled web apps that agents can use through browsers and MCP tools.

faq.question: Does it require a specific backend stack?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use Node.js, TypeScript, Express, SQLite, @longrun/turtle, and ATXP packages.

faq.question: Can it add payments to MCP tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows a paid tool pattern using ATXP authentication and payment checks.

faq.question: Is the cookie pattern production-ready?
faq.answer: No. The template needs stronger token handling, logging controls, expiration, and revocation before production use.

faq.question: Does it create a full frontend?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on server, authentication, MCP, and publishing patterns for an agent-facing app.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
